subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with a narrower passing command set such as `pnpm check:docs`?
rationale: The issue fits OpenClaw test-infrastructure goals, but the exact recurring Windows command set changes CI cost and the active PR has failing proof for one selected command.

options.title: Prove Full Smoke Before Merge
options.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after `check:docs` and `build:strict-smoke` both pass in the Windows `pwsh` lane with redacted proof.

options.title: Start Narrower
options.body: Land a smaller native PowerShell smoke for commands already proven on Windows and track build-smoke coverage separately.

options.title: Defer Recurring Coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the PR until Windows runner budget and build-smoke ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Prove Full Smoke Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after `check:docs` and `build:strict-smoke` both pass in the Windows `pwsh` lane with redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent overlap between CI workflow work and the PowerShell-safe docs command path.
